# Real PNG 1.2 §5 file structure — 8-byte signature, then chunks REPEATED UNTIL the `IEND`
# tag (not count-prefixed): `len(u32 BE) + type(4 ASCII) + data + crc32(u32 BE)`, tag-dispatched
# into wholly different field shapes per chunk type, ALL BIG-ENDIAN — matching this artifact's
# real `read_chunks`/`write_chunk` (📷️png/…/⚙️engine/🦀️component.rs:30-77) field-for-field. This
# is P2-M2's own worked PNG example (`p2-m2-report.md` item 1) extended to every chunk kind this
# artifact's real decoder actually types.
#
# This is the SEMIO-envelope-UNWRAPPED payload (P2-M3 §3/§5 point 4) — `PngSnapshot::
# encode_pack_with` (../../🦀️component.rs) is `encode_png(self)` wrapped by `store::
# semio_format::wrap_binary`, so the bytes this file walks start exactly where the envelope's
# own 8-byte magic + u32le token-length + token hand off (described once, framework-side, at
# 🧰️framework/…/🧬️semio/📡️protocol/📡️component.protocol.semio) — NOT re-described here.
#
# `framing magic 0x89504E470D0A1A0A` is PNG's own real 8-byte signature (§5.2) — the ONE
# construct in this dialect that is actually byte-checked at walk time (`walk_protocol`'s
# `Framing::Magic` arm), giving real validation instead of an unchecked `header fixed 8` skip.
framing magic 0x89504E470D0A1A0A

repeat chunks {
tag fixed 4
length u32be
order length-first
trailer u32be
until "IEND"

# §11.2.2 IHDR — always exactly 13 bytes, unconditional, every field genuinely typed.
# `compression`/`filter` are validated-but-fixed-at-0 by the real decoder (`parse_ihdr`) —
# still modeled as real fields here since they ARE real bytes on the wire, just constrained.
arm "IHDR" {
width u32be
height u32be
bit_depth u8
color_type u8
compression u8
filter u8
interlace u8
}

# §11.2.3 PLTE — a variable-length run of 3-byte RGB entries (`palette.len() * 3` bytes,
# no count field of its own on the wire — the entry count is `length / 3`, and this dialect's
# `Array` count source is a NAMED FIELD (`Count::Field`), not an arithmetic expression over
# `length`, which this `repeat` block's own `length` read never binds to a name in the walk
# env in the first place — confirmed unchanged since P2-M2, see this artifact's report
# `mechanism_gaps`). Left as a genuinely opaque, honestly-bounded arm: `walk_repeat` already
# auto-skips exactly `length` declared bytes for ANY arm whose fields under-consume it (see
# `walk_repeat`'s `expected_end` handling, `📖️grammar/🦀️component.rs`) — the SAME mechanism
# that skips a wholly UNRECOGNIZED chunk type, just named here for self-documentation since
# the real decoder DOES specifically recognize and type this chunk (`plte_out`,
# `⚙️engine/🦀️component.rs:567-573`).
arm "PLTE" { }

# §11.3.3 tRNS — shape depends on `color_type` (decoded by IHDR, earlier in this SAME walk,
# now resolvable via P2-M2 item 3's cross-block field env): grayscale is a fixed 2-byte
# `u16be`, truecolor a fixed 6-byte RGB16, indexed a variable per-palette-entry alpha run
# (bounded only by `length`, same "no named length" gap as PLTE above). Modeling a per-tag
# INNER dispatch (grayscale vs truecolor vs indexed) would need a SECOND conditional layer
# keyed off a value this dialect has no way to always-guarantee-decoded when the OUTER
# `color_type` doesn't match — `Cond`'s `eval_cond` hard-errors if its guarded field was
# itself only conditionally read (confirmed by reading `eval_cond`/`walk_fields`) — so this
# arm stays one honest opaque skip rather than a half-correct partial dispatch (see this
# artifact's report `mechanism_gaps`, "protocol-cond-cannot-chain").
arm "tRNS" { }

# §11.3.5.2 gAMA — always exactly 4 bytes, one real BE u32 field.
arm "gAMA" { gamma u32be }

# §11.3.5.2 cHRM — always exactly 32 bytes, 8 real BE u32 fields (white/red/green/blue x/y).
arm "cHRM" {
white_x u32be
white_y u32be
red_x u32be
red_y u32be
green_x u32be
green_y u32be
blue_x u32be
blue_y u32be
}

# §11.3.5.3 sRGB — always exactly 1 byte, one real u8 rendering-intent field.
arm "sRGB" { intent u8 }

# §11.3.5.4 pHYs — always exactly 9 bytes, three real fields.
arm "pHYs" {
ppu_x u32be
ppu_y u32be
unit u8
}

# §11.3.6.1 tIME — always exactly 7 bytes, six real fields.
arm "tIME" {
year u16be
month u8
day u8
hour u8
minute u8
second u8
}

# §11.3.5.1 bKGD — shape depends on `color_type` (grayscale=2 bytes / truecolor=6 bytes /
# indexed=1 byte), same per-tag-inner-dispatch limitation as tRNS above — one honest opaque
# skip (real decoder still types it, `bkgd_out`, `⚙️engine/🦀️component.rs:647-674`).
arm "bKGD" { }

# §11.3.4 tEXt/zTXt/iTXt — NUL-delimited keyword + (optionally zlib-compressed) value; the
# NUL terminator isn't a fixed-width scalar this dialect can scan for (no "read until byte
# value" primitive distinct from `MarkerScan`'s own fixed-fill-byte-then-one-byte shape), and
# zTXt/iTXt's payload is itself a compressed bitstream — an honest opaque skip for all three
# real text-chunk kinds (typed by the real decoder, `text_chunks`, `⚙️engine/🦀️component.rs
# :675-718`).
arm "tEXt" { }
arm "zTXt" { }
arm "iTXt" { }

# §11.2.4 IDAT — the compressed image data itself; opaque by the user's own "compressed
# payload" carve-out (deflate bitstream, not byte/Prim-granular — matches this program's
# 🗜️deflate artifact's own documented boundary).
arm "IDAT" { }

# §11.2.5 IEND — always exactly 0 bytes; also this `repeat` block's `until` sentinel.
arm "IEND" { }
}

Feature: Apply every typed PNG 1.2 mutation to a real-world document
  The input is a real 250 KB, 2334x2560, 8-bit COLORMAP architectural floor plan
  (rathaus-ahlen-grundriss.png), not a synthetic fixture — it exercises the PLTE/palette decode
  path, not just RGBA. Walking its chunk chain gives exactly IHDR (colour type 3, bit depth 8,
  non-interlaced), PLTE (233 entries), eight IDAT chunks and IEND: no tRNS, no gAMA/cHRM/sRGB/pHYs,
  no tIME, no bKGD, no text chunk, no private chunk. Every scenario copies it into the case work
  directory before touching it; the committed document is never written to.

  Three kinds address an EXISTING text or unknown chunk, and the real document carries neither, so
  remove-text-chunk, set-text-chunk and remove-unknown-chunk are exercised on the real document
  after the reference implementation has inserted their target first — the same arrange step the
  OOXML conformance cases use for their own removal kinds. Anything else would be a row whose
  parameters address nothing, which passes without testing anything.

  The oracle applies each mutation independently against the registered `png` reference crate's own
  Encoder/Decoder API; the subject fully parses the artifact into the typed `PngSnapshot` and
  re-serializes from it. Both results are read back by the INDEPENDENT `png` decoder. The compared
  projection is the WHOLE document, not just its raster: geometry and a digest of the decoded RGBA
  samples (PNG is lossless, so a digest is an exact claim), plus the palette, the five typed
  ancillary chunks, the timestamp, the background colour, the text chunks by keyword and value, and
  the private chunks by type and payload digest. tIME and private chunks come from a fixed-grammar
  walk over §5.3's chunk chain, because `png::Info` models neither.

  ⚠️ Two of the seventeen kinds genuinely cannot reach the bytes, and the case says so rather than
  letting them pass as though they had:
    – set-header — IHDR must describe the IDAT that follows it, and both encoders always write
      colour type 6 / bit depth 8 / interlace 0 because `PngSnapshot.pixels` is a canonical RGBA
      buffer (`encode_png`'s own 🚫️EncodeScopeNote). `SetHeader` also does not resize `pixels`, so
      changing width or height would only make the snapshot unencodable. Every field of this kind
      is model-only.

      both encoders write, the chunk can never appear. `encode_png` used to emit it anyway from the
      snapshot, producing a file the reference decoder rejects outright (`ColorWithBadTrns`); it now
      omits it, with the source's alpha already resolved into `pixels`.
  Both are named in the adapter's observability exemption list. Every other kind must move the
  projection, and the oracle fails the scenario if it does not.

# dialect, `%x` ranges, `/` alternation -- none of it this dialect's real syntax). Matches this
# artifact's own real encoder field-for-field (⚙️engine/component.rs `encode_jpg`/
# `encode_jfif_app0`/`write_dht`) for the fixed, non-arithmetic-dependent portion of every marker
# segment -- ITU-T T.81/ISO 10918-1 + JFIF 1.02 (ITU-T T.871). `walk_protocol` is tested (this
# artifact's own `protocol_walk_law`) against `unwrap_binary(encode_pack(demo_jpg_snapshot()))` --
# i.e. REAL `encode_jpg` output -- not a hand-fabricated fixture.
#
# `framing record` (not `framing magic`): `framing magic` always reads/compares exactly 8 raw
# bytes (`magic_bytes(u64)`, confirmed by direct read of `walk_protocol`'s `Framing::Magic` arm),
# but JPEG's SOI is only 2 bytes (0xFFD8) -- forcing an 8-byte compare would misalign against the
# very next marker's own leading bytes. SOI is modeled as an ordinary 2-byte header field instead
# (still genuinely, individually walked -- just not via the magic-framing shortcut).

header fixed 2

# P2-FG2 mechanism gap (new -- not yet in the recipe's §5 consolidated table; recorded here AND in
# this wave's report for the periodic table-consolidation pass): `repeat`'s own `length <prim>`
# directive computes `expected_end = body_start + length` -- i.e. it assumes an EXCLUSIVE length
# (PNG/GIF convention: `length` = bytes AFTER the length field itself). JPEG's own `Lp` field is
# INCLUSIVE of the two length bytes themselves (T.81 §B.1.1.4) -- declaring `length` at the
# `repeat` dispatch level (or feeding it into an `Array(_, Field(name))` count) would overcount
# every segment's real remaining body by exactly 2 bytes and eat the next marker's leading
# `0xFF`+type byte, corrupting the walk. No subtraction/arithmetic primitive exists anywhere in
# this dialect (`Cond` only tests equality against a literal, `Field(name)` binds a decoded count
# verbatim, no `-2` adjustment is expressible) -- confirmed by direct read of
# `walk_repeat`/`walk_fields`/`resolve_count`, not guessed. Worked around below: `length` is
# declared as an ORDINARY field in every arm (genuinely, individually decoded -- just never used to

# primitive" root cause as above, both sidestepped by this artifact's own conformance fixture
# rather than fixed:
#  - APP0's thumbnail RGB payload (`thumb_width * thumb_height * 3` bytes) needs a PRODUCT of two

#    silently mismodeled.
#  - `other_segments` (generic retained APPn/COM markers) has a length-prefixed OPAQUE body whose
#    true remaining byte count is `Lp - 2` -- the SAME inclusive-length problem the main comment

#    the opaque content). `demo_jpg_snapshot()` carries no `other_segments`, so no such marker ever

# nothing past it (`trailing_reserved` walks blocks AFTER this one and stops at the next
# structural block, confirmed by direct read of `walk_protocol`'s per-block `reserved` computation).
segment entropy {
scan_data bytes

# trailer get (`📖️grammar-recipe.md` §6): the real value is always exactly `0xFFD9` but this

  ONE decode and re-encode by the reference — and not against the committed bytes. JPEG is lossy and

  scanner's, so a single decode/re-encode already moves the raster and replaces the DQT. Measuring
  against the untouched scan would fold that unavoidable normalization into every scenario, making
  every kind look observable and every inverse look broken, both for the same reason and neither
  about the mutation.

  one decode/re-encode at quality 90 moves at most 2018 pixels between luma buckets, a pass through
  quality 50 at most 10 014 and through quality 5 at most 55 570 — all far inside it — while the
  set-pixels and set-snapshot rows displace ~5.6 million pixels, an order of magnitude past it.
  Exact per-bucket equality is a law JPEG does not have and is deliberately not asserted.

  Walking the fixture's own marker chain gives APP0 (JFIF, version 1.1, density unit 1 = dots per
  inch, 500x500), APP1 carrying a real 31,385-byte Adobe XMP packet, two DQT, SOF0, four DHT and
  SOS. That real APP1 is what remove-other-segment removes and what insert-other-segment is inserted
  in front of; neither row addresses something the file does not have.

  DRI/restart marker at all.

  set-restart-interval mutate only the in-memory typed snapshot — none of the five is observable in
  the re-serialized bytes, by design, not by test gap. They are the ONLY five kinds named in the
  adapter's observability exemption list, and every other kind is required to move the compared
  projection or its scenario fails.

  set-jfif-header, insert-other-segment and remove-other-segment ARE written to real bytes — a real

# P2-FG2: real M2 protocol dialect, replacing the pre-M2 ABNF-styled placeholder this file used
# to hold. Per M3's own guidance (`p2-m3-report.md` §5 point 4 / this ticket's own recipe §2.1):
# "model it as if the bytes you're walking already start at the payload" -- the SEMIO binary
# envelope (`store::semio_format::wrap_binary`/`unwrap_binary`) is described ONCE, framework-side
# (`semio.envelope`), and is stripped BEFORE `walk_protocol` ever sees these bytes (confirmed by
# reading `m5_handcrafted_protocol_conformance::inner_payload_from_semio_example`, which
# `unwrap_binary`s the real `.pack.semio` fixture first) -- this file does NOT re-describe it.
#
# What remains is the REAL on-disk BMP byte stream `engine::decode_bmp`/`encode_bmp`
# (../../../⚙️engine/🦀️component.rs) read/write field-by-field: BITMAPFILEHEADER (14 bytes) +
# the 40-byte BITMAPINFOHEADER core (11 real fields, header_size>=40 is honestly modeled, but
# only the CLASSIC 40-byte core is field-by-field -- the same documented scope cut
# `decode_bmp`/`encode_bmp` themselves make for V2-V5 extended headers, header_size>40) +
# conditional BI_BITFIELDS masks + conditional palette + trailing pixel data.
#
# `framing magic` cannot honestly represent BMP's real signature: `Framing::Magic` always reads
# and compares exactly 8 bytes (`magic_bytes`/`walk_protocol`'s `Framing::Magic` arm,
# 📖️grammar/🦀️component.rs), but BMP's real on-disk magic is only 2 bytes ("BM",
# `engine::BMP_MAGIC`) immediately followed by a real, non-zero `file_size` field -- there is no
# way to zero-pad "BM" out to 8 bytes and have it match real file bytes 2..8 (unlike PNG, whose
# OWN 8-byte signature happens to fill the primitive exactly). This is a genuine dialect gap
# (recorded as `mechanism_gaps` id `protocol-magic-shorter-than-8-bytes` in this wave's own
# report) shared by every OTHER short-magic binary-native format in this same wave (gif87a/89a's
# 6-byte "GIF87a"/"GIF89a", jpg's 2-byte 0xFFD8, tiff's 2-byte "II"/"MM"). Honest workaround used
# here, matching `binary`/raw's own "no structure to assert" precedent: `framing record`, and
# model the 2 magic bytes as a genuine, individually-walked (but content-UNVALIDATED by this
# dialect) `fixed 2` field -- deep content validation (`bytes[0..2] == b"BM"`) stays Rust-side,
# same division of labor the dialect already gives every checksum/CRC (structurally irreducible
# at the protocol-description layer, not silently skipped).
framing record

header fixed 14
field bmp_magic fixed 2
field file_size u32
field reserved1 u16
field reserved2 u16
field data_offset u32

# The 40-byte BITMAPINFOHEADER core, unconditional (always present per `decode_bmp`'s own
# `header_size < 40` rejection) -- every field individually, honestly walked, in real on-disk
# order (`decode_bmp` offsets 14+0..14+40).
segment info_header {
  header_size u32
  width i32
  height i32
  planes u16
  bits_per_pixel u16
  compression u32
  image_size u32
  x_pixels_per_meter i32
  y_pixels_per_meter i32
  colors_used u32
  colors_important u32
}

# BI_BITFIELDS (`compression == 3`) 16/32bpp channel masks -- M2's conditional-presence
# construct, gated on `compression` (decoded by the earlier `info_header` segment, resolved via
# M2's cross-block field-env threading). Models the classic Win9x 3-DWORD-mask extension
# (`decode_bmp`'s `header_size == 40` branch) only -- the OPTIONAL 4th (alpha) mask is gated in
# the real codec by a POSITION comparison (`cursor + 4 <= data_offset`), which this dialect's
# `Cond` cannot express (`Cond` compares one earlier field against a fixed constant, never two
# runtime values against each other) -- recorded as `mechanism_gaps` id
# `protocol-cond-field-vs-field` below; the real committed `.pack.semio` fixture never exercises
# BI_BITFIELDS (encode_bmp is scope-cut to 24-bit BI_RGB only, see `EncodeScopeNote`) so this
# never blocks `protocol_walk_law`. The BITMAPV2/V3/V4/V5INFOHEADER in-header mask placement
# (`header_size >= 56`) is the SAME documented "only the 40-byte core is field-by-field" scope
# cut as `decode_bmp` itself makes.
segment bitfield_masks if compression eq 3 {
  mask_r u32
  mask_g u32
  mask_b u32
}

# Color palette, present only when `bits_per_pixel <= 8` (M2 conditional-presence segment) --
# a real count-from-field repeated structure (M2 cross-block field-env threading), not opaque:
# `colors_used` entries, each a real 4-byte (b,g,r,reserved) span. `decode_bmp`'s own real count
# formula additionally falls back to `1 << bits_per_pixel` when `colors_used == 0` (the common
# "full default palette" case) -- `Count::Field` only resolves a DIRECT field value, with no
# conditional-default arithmetic, so that fallback is not expressible here (`mechanism_gaps` id
# `protocol-count-field-no-default`); the real committed fixture is 24bpp (no palette at all,
# segment absent) so this never blocks `protocol_walk_law` either. Each entry stays one opaque
# 4-byte span (b/g/r/reserved not broken into named sub-fields) since `Array`'s own inner `Prim`
# is a single scalar/fixed type, never a multi-field record (`protocol-array-of-records`, this
# ticket's own recipe §5).
segment palette if bits_per_pixel le 8 {
  entries Array(Fixed(4), Field(colors_used))
}

# Pixel data: row-padded-to-4-byte-boundary DIB rows (`row_bytes = ((width*bpp+31)/32)*4`),
# bottom-up by default (top-down when `height` was negative -- BOTH already captured, honestly,
# by `row_order`'s real sign read above; the physical row DIRECTION and the per-row PADDING
# stride are real, Rust-side facts this dialect has no computed-arithmetic primitive to restate
# -- `Count`/`Array` only take a literal/varint/direct-field count, never a formula over two
# fields -- so, per this ticket's own brief, the payload stays one opaque trailing byte run; the
# stride formula is documented here rather than silently omitted). Always the LAST block, so it
# can honestly consume "rest of buffer" with no length prefix.
chain pixel_data bytes

# `scalar_to_text` (🗣️dsl/🧬️schema/🦀️component.rs) prints a `String` field bare (`IDENT`) when it
# lexes back as exactly one identifier (`is_bare_ident` — the lexer's ident alphabet includes
# `.`/`-`/`_`/`/`, so e.g. `stdio.bmp` prints bare), quoted+escaped (`TEXT`) otherwise -- base64
# payloads (`#[dsl(base64)]` fields, below) always fall to the quoted `TEXT` form in practice
# (base64's own alphabet routinely includes `+`/`/`/`=`, which `is_bare_ident` rejects).

row-order-value = "bottom-up" | "top-down"

# `SetSnapshot`'s whole `BmpSnapshot` payload is `#[dsl(block)]` -- printed as
# `snapshot { ... }` (`Shape::Block(Shape::Record(...))`). Field order inside, verified against a

snapshot-fields = schema-field header-size-field width-field height-field row-order-field planes-field bits-per-pixel-field compression-field image-size-field x-ppm-field y-ppm-field colors-used-field colors-important-field snapshot-pixels-field snapshot-palette-field

height-field = "height" "=" INT

colors-important-field = "colors-important" "=" INT

# P2-FG2: REAL binary diff frame, replacing F6's `print_diff().into_bytes()` text-as-binary
# shortcut (`../../🦀️component.rs`'s old `DiffCodec::encode_diff` -- per the P2-W0 census, 100%
# of stdio's `DiffCodec` impls were still on this shortcut). `format u8` + `flags u8` (bit0 =
# `byte_order` present, bit1 = `ifds` present, bit2 = `pixels` present -- `TiffDiff` has THREE
# independently-optional top-level fields, same shape `XmlDiff`'s own bitmask needed) as two REAL
# fixed fields, individually protocol-walked.
#
# Past that header, `byte_order`/`ifds`/`pixels` (whichever `flags` marks present, in that FIXED
# order) are bundled into ONE opaque trailing `bytes` chain rather than three separately-declared
# conditional fields: this dialect's `Cond` (`if flags eq N`) can only test a field's WHOLE value
# against a literal, not an individual BIT of it (no bitwise-AND primitive exists,
# `📖️grammar-recipe.md` §2.2's own `Cond` section), so a per-bit-guarded field list isn't
# expressible here even before `ifds`' own shape is considered. And `ifds`' own payload
# (`TiffIfdsDiff` nesting `TiffTagsDiff` nesting the 12-variant `TiffValues` union) is a
# repeated, per-entry-varying-shape RECORD collection -- the `protocol-array-of-records`
# mechanism gap (§5), the same root cause ZIP's/CSV's own nested-record-array collections hit --
# so once ANY field of this frame is structurally unwalkable at this dialect's field-by-field
# depth, bundling the two simpler, merely-optional fields (`byte_order`/`pixels`) into the SAME
# opaque tail, instead of partially structuring only those two, is the honest, minimal-surface
# choice: the Rust `encode_diff`/`decode_diff` side stays genuinely, fully structured (bit-tested,
# individually typed, real varint-framed binary recursion through `enc_ifds_diff_bin`/
# `enc_tags_diff_bin`/`enc_values_bin`) and round-trip tested independently.
framing record
header fixed 2
field format u8
field flags u8
chain payload bytes

# P2-FG2: real one-line `DiffCodec::print_diff`/`parse_diff` shape ALREADY emitted by
# `../../🦀️component.rs` (`print_tiff_diff`/`parse_tiff_diff`), replacing the F6-era placeholder
# that described neither the real snapshot NOR the real diff wire shape. Every keyword/tag token
# below is copied verbatim from the real `format!(...)` call sites, not invented.
#
# `comment none`: not strictly required by any token this grammar's own alphabet produces (hex
# payloads are lowercase-only, never containing `#`), kept for consistency with the sibling
# ../../📸️snapshot/📝️text grammar.
#
# `hex` (bare `hex`, referenced below but deliberately NOT defined as a production in this file)
# is the framework's built-in `hex` MACRO — see the mandatory-macro rationale in
# `📖️grammar-recipe.md` §1.3(f)/§3 pitfall 2 (a hand-rolled `{INT|IDENT}*` production never
# backtracks and would silently swallow a following bareword literal like `ifds`/`pixels`).
document = byte-order-tok? ifds-tok? pixels-tok?
byte-order-tok = "byte-order" "=" byte-order-lit
byte-order-lit = "0" | "1"
ifds-tok = "ifds" "=" ifds-diff-body
pixels-tok = "pixels" "=" hex

# `enc_ifds_diff`/`dec_ifds_diff` -- `[removed];[modified];[added]`, index-keyed (TIFF's own IFD
# chain is positional, `📖️grammar-recipe.md` §1.4's index-keyed collection-triple shape).
# `modified` entries are `index:<tags-diff-body>` (recursive), `added` entries are
# `index:<ifd-lit>`.
ifds-diff-body = "[" removed-list? "]" ";" "[" ifd-modified-list? "]" ";" "[" ifd-added-list? "]"
removed-list = INT {"," INT}*
ifd-modified-list = ifd-modified-item {"," ifd-modified-item}*
ifd-modified-item = INT ":" tags-diff-body
ifd-added-list = ifd-added-item {"," ifd-added-item}*
ifd-added-item = INT ":" ifd-lit

# `enc_tags_diff`/`dec_tags_diff` -- `[removed];[modified];[added]`, TAG-ID-keyed (a TIFF tag id
# is TIFF's own natural stable identity within one IFD, not an ordinal position). `modified`/
# `added` entries are `tag:kind:values` (colon-separated -- safe since `kind` is bare decimal and
# `values` never contains a literal `:`).
tags-diff-body = "[" removed-list? "]" ";" "[" tag-modified-list? "]" ";" "[" tag-added-list? "]"
tag-modified-list = tag-modified-item {"," tag-modified-item}*
tag-modified-item = INT ":" INT ":" tiff-values
tag-added-list = tag-added-item {"," tag-added-item}*
tag-added-item = INT ":" INT ":" tiff-values

# `enc_ifd`/`dec_ifd`/`enc_tag`/`dec_tag` -- restated here (same shape as
# ../../📸️snapshot's real tag/type/value model) so this leaf grammar is self-contained, matching
# the repo's existing per-facet convention. `enc_list`'s uniform bracketed-comma-list shape
# (`📖️grammar-recipe.md`'s own `hex` macro companion pattern).
ifd-lit = "[" ifd-entry-list? "]"
ifd-entry-list = tag-lit {"," tag-lit}*
tag-lit = "[" INT "," INT "," tiff-values "]"

# `enc_values`/`dec_values` -- single-uppercase-letter tag prefix immediately followed by the
# bracketed positional payload (same convention `xml`'s `enc_xml_node`/gif's enum codecs use):
# `B`=Byte, `A`=Ascii, `S`=Short, `L`=Long, `R`=Rational, `E`=SByte, `U`=Undefined, `H`=SShort,
# `G`=SLong, `Q`=SRational, `F`=Float, `D`=Double. `Byte`/`Undefined` (raw octets) and `Ascii`
# (text) are hex; every numeric list is decimal (or float) comma-separated;
# `Rational`/`SRational` pairs nest as `[n,d]`.
tiff-values = "B" "[" hex "]" | "A" "[" hex "]" | "S" number-list | "L" number-list | "R" rational-list | "E" number-list | "U" "[" hex "]" | "H" number-list | "G" number-list | "Q" rational-list | "F" number-list | "D" number-list
number-list = "[" number-comma-list? "]"
number-comma-list = number {"," number}*
# Rust's `f32`/`f64` `Display` prints an integer-valued float (e.g. `3.0`) WITHOUT a decimal
# point (`"3"`), so a `Float`/`Double` list can genuinely lex either token kind alongside a
# signed/unsigned integer list's always-`INT` tokens -- same `NUMBER = FLOAT | INT` shape the
# recipe's own STEP-value worked example uses (§1.3(e)).
number = FLOAT | INT
rational-list = "[" rational-comma-list? "]"
rational-comma-list = rational-item {"," rational-item}*
rational-item = "[" number "," number "]"
